notes: Real headless-browser run against live TicTacToeDuel sample (:5000, Postgres :5433, Redis :6379). description: RankAdjustDialog palette flow (ladder selector + rating field + audit row)
notes: Opened the palette, filtered to the rank-adjust verb, searched for seeded player "UAT-RankAdjustTarget" (11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111), selected it — RankAdjustDialog opened with the ladder selector populated from live /admin/api data (2 active ladders: main, tictactoe) and the numeric rating field present with server-configured Min/Max bounds. Submitted New Rating=1800 with a valid 3-512 char reason; dialog closed on success (no validation error surfaced). DB verification (evidence/db-verification-log.txt) confirms exactly ONE admin.player.rank_adjust audit row for the target player with the submitted reason text, and the player_ranks row now shows Rating=1800 (matches submission) on the ladder used.

description: Live account merge via Admin UI (POST /admin/api/players/merge)
notes: Authenticated via POST /admin/api/login (gk_admin_session cookie), harvested __RequestVerificationToken from GET /admin/login, sent it as X-GameKit-Admin-CSRF. POST /admin/api/players/merge with sourcePlayerId=44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444 (UAT-MergeSource2) and targetPlayerId=55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555 (UAT-MergeTarget2) returned HTTP 200 {targetPlayerId, status:"merged"} (SourcePlayerId correctly absent from the response per SC#5/T-10-04-03). DB verification confirms the source player row is tombstoned (MergedIntoPlayerId set to the target, DeletedAt set) and exactly ONE auth.account_merge audit row exists, keyed by TargetId=<target player id> (not source, per the audit schema).

description: Idempotent second identical merge (same source+target -> already_merged)
notes: Repeated the identical POST /admin/api/players/merge (same source+target ids, same CSRF-protected session) immediately after item 3. Returned HTTP 200 {targetPlayerId, status:"already_merged"}. DB verification confirms still exactly ONE auth.account_merge audit row (no duplicate created by the second call) and exactly ONE auth.logout.all row for the source player (token revocation happened only once, not re-triggered by the idempotent replay).
